criteria.evidence: I read the diff. The CHANGELOG Unreleased/Added item says 'Root cause: the reading stage had no step asking who performs each action, where, with what permissions, and what data it reaches' and cites all three jobs. The doc comment at reading.rs:4273-4327 says the same and also cites the three introspections. The test environment_reach_doc_and_changelog_name_the_cause checks both texts and passed when I ran it.

criteria.criterion: `refusing_check` in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs contains a single `step!(check_environment_reach(..))` line, and crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs lists the rule so the reader is told to write an `Environment:` assumption.
criteria.evidence: reading.rs:3250 is `step!(check_environment_reach(reading));`. The test environment_reach_has_one_step_line checks there is exactly one such line, directly after check_outcome_state, and it passed. READING_RULES in briefs.rs grows to 7 entries; the new line names `Environment:` and `check_environment_reach`, and the updated brief test passed.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core`: unit tests show a reading that adds a CI workflow deliverable, or a push/pull-request/gh action, without an `Environment:` assumption naming site, permissions and reachable data is refused by `check_environment_reach`, and the same reading with such an assumption is accepted. These tests fail when the new step is removed.
criteria.evidence: These tests passed: environment_reach_refuses_a_workflow_deliverable_without_an_environment (Create and Modify are refused, Delete is not), environment_reach_refuses_each_host_action_without_an_environment (15 phrasings, each refused through refusing_check with the check's name and accepted once CI_ENVIRONMENT is added), and environment_reach_needs_a_site_a_permission_and_the_data. They assert refuser()==Some("check_environment_reach") through refusing_check, so removing the step line makes them fail. Athena's revert run failed to compile (exit 101) because the function itself was reverted; that also counts as failing without the change.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core`: a test shows a reading citing job records, history or the records branch as a source is refused unless the figures are quoted inline or an `Environment:` assumption lists a reachable file, and that it is accepted when they are. Tests cover the class (separate readings shaped like each of the three jobs), not one job.

findings.summary: A write to the records branch in a behavior criterion does not trigger the check unless the subject is exactly `CI`.
findings.evidence: C1 fires only when a read verb comes before the source. 'The record is written in the records branch' is accepted on purpose (it is a fixture), and so would 'Athena writes the record to the records branch' be. Yet the engm case was about which place can write records. A narrow fix: treat write/commit/push verbs before 'records branch' as a host action. The fixture shows the gap is deliberate, but the doc comment's Limits section does not mention it.

findings.summary: A push to a host named by its brand is missed.
findings.evidence: The words that count as a push target are origin, remote, upstream, branch(es) and ref(s). So 'Athena pushes to GitHub' or 'pushes the tag to GitHub' does not trigger. Adding github, gitlab and tag to the target list would close the gap at little false-positive cost.

findings.summary: The declared 8% share is well above the measured replay result.
findings.evidence: Both texts say 'expected 8% of newly refused readings' and label it an unmeasured estimate. Athena's replay counted 0 of 50 newly refused. The estimate is labelled honestly; the text could be updated once the measurement is in.
findings.location: CHANGELOG.md; reading.rs doc comment on check_environment_reach

summary: The change adds `check_environment_reach` to the reading gate in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs. It runs as one `step!` line in `refusing_check`, right after `check_outcome_state`. It refuses a reading that does any of these without a complete `Environment:` assumption naming the site, its read/write permissions and the data it reaches: adds or changes a CI workflow, puts a host action in a behavior criterion (git/gh command, push to a ref or origin, opening or merging a PR, a GitHub API call, a CI write), or reads the records branch or git history in one. When the site is a local working copy and the action is a host action, the assumption must also say what happens with no origin. A summary that cites job records or history needs counted figures in an assumption, or a reachable file listed in an `Environment:` assumption. This matches the request: the fix sits at the reading stage, where the cause starts, not in any one job. The doc comment and the CHANGELOG entry both name the cause and the three jobs. The reader brief gains one rule line. The refusal corpus gains 19 cases and 7 input-form tags. I ran `cargo test -p athena-core environment_reach` (13 unit tests and the corpus declaration test passed), `cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus` (13 passed) and `cargo test -p athena-context the_reader_brief_names_each_reading_rule_in_one_short_line` (passed). The recorded fmt, clippy and test runs passed in CI. Only the four expected files changed. The check works by matching words, which the reading planned and the doc comment states. It has two minor false negatives, listed in the findings. The declared 8% refusal share is labelled as an unmeasured estimate. Athena's replay counted 0 of 50 accepted readings newly refused.
